userStories.title: Extract manifest types to create file-size headroom
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Relocate the manifest and chunk declarations into a dedicated module while preserving their public imports and runtime persistence behavior.

**Motivation** — `src/context/engine/types.ts` is at **590 lines**, leaving 10 lines of headroom, and this feature adds an import plus two documented optional fields there.

**Approach** — US-001 is a **pure move** — no behaviour change, no new code. It relocates the manifest/chunk type block (`ChunkEffectiveness`, `ContextChunk`, `ContextManifest`, lines 123-320) out of `src/context/engine/types.ts` into a new `src/context/engine/manifest-types.ts`, re-exported from `types.ts` so no import site changes. This drops `types.ts` to roughly 395 lines, giving US-004 room to add its fields.

**Scope** — In: move only `ChunkEffectiveness`, `ContextChunk`, and `ContextManifest`; retain type dependencies and re-export the moved names from `types.ts`; preserve manifest-store read/write behavior. Out: adding `budgetPressure`, changing provider results, modifying packing, or changing manifest write concurrency (belongs to US-004 or is feature-out-of-scope).

**Interface** — `ContextManifest` remains importable from `src/context/engine/types.ts` after the move.
acceptanceCriteria: When `ContextManifest` is imported from `src/context/engine/types.ts`, then a manifest value constructed against it is accepted by `writeContextManifest` without error.
When a manifest is written through `writeContextManifest` and read through `loadContextManifests`, then its `includedChunks` equals the written value.
When a manifest is written through `writeContextManifest` and read through `loadContextManifests`, then its `providerResults` equals the written value.
When the injected manifest-store `writeFile` rejects during `writeContextManifest`, then `writeContextManifest` rejects with that failure after the type move.

routing.reasoning: A bounded mechanical extraction and re-export with no new behavior or dependency.
routing.noTestJustification: This is a pure type-declaration move with no intended runtime behavior change; existing manifest persistence tests and automatic static gates verify the preserved export and file-size constraint.

userStories.title: Implement soft canonical-rules budget with opt-in enforcement
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make canonical rules budgeting advisory by default while retaining the existing contiguous-tail truncation behind explicit enforcement.

**Motivation** — The canonical-rules provider currently discards rules that do not fit a fixed 8,192-token ceiling, silently losing roughly half of this repository's rule corpus before the packer ever runs.

**Approach** — Two implementations were considered. This spec chooses **soft-by-default**, not **raise-the-constant**.

Raising `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES_BUDGET_TOKENS` to a larger number only moves the cliff, and the cliff returns silently as the corpus grows. Making the ceiling advisory eliminates the cliff permanently and resolves the contradiction in Motivation #1 — rules are floor-kind (`packing.ts:36`), so a hard pre-pack drop contradicts the packer's own semantics one layer down.

`budgetTokens` is therefore reinterpreted as a **reporting threshold** rather than a guillotine. Its numeric default is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: extend the canonical budget result and function, add `enforceBudget` to schema/runtime config, and update both nested config default literals. Out: provider emission and provider budget-pressure reporting (US-003); manifest/metrics propagation (US-004); changes to `packChunks`, `FLOOR_KINDS` membership, floor-overflow semantics, or any per-stage `budgetTokens` value in `stage-config.ts`.

**Interface** — `applyCanonicalRulesBudget(rules, budgetTokens)` gains a third parameter `options?: { enforce?: boolean }`. `CanonicalRulesBudgetResult` gains `overageTokens: number`. `ContextV2RulesConfigSchema` and `ContextV2RulesConfig` gain `enforceBudget: boolean`, defaulting to false. For a finite, positive threshold in soft mode, preserve every supplied rule and use total token count as used tokens; for enforced mode preserve the existing leading-rules-that-fit algorithm. Invalid zero, negative, and non-finite budgets retain the existing empty-result behavior. `overageTokens` is `max(0, totalTokens - budgetTokens)` for valid thresholds.
acceptanceCriteria: When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules whose total exceeds `budgetTokens` and `enforce` is false, then it returns every supplied rule.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules whose total exceeds `budgetTokens` and `enforce` is false, then it returns `droppedCount` equal to 0.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules whose total exceeds `budgetTokens` and `enforce` is false, then it returns `overageTokens` equal to total rule tokens minus `budgetTokens`.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules whose total exceeds `budgetTokens` and `enforce` is false, then it returns `usedTokens` equal to `totalTokens`.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules exceeding `budgetTokens` with `enforce` true, then it returns only leading rules whose cumulative tokens fit within `budgetTokens`.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules exceeding `budgetTokens` with `enforce` true, then it returns `droppedCount` equal to the number of remaining rules.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives rules whose total is less than or equal to `budgetTokens`, then it returns `overageTokens` equal to 0.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives `budgetTokens` of 0, then it returns no rules and `droppedCount` equal to the number of supplied rules.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives a negative `budgetTokens`, then it returns no rules and `droppedCount` equal to the number of supplied rules.
When `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` receives a non-finite `budgetTokens`, then it returns no rules and `droppedCount` equal to the number of supplied rules.
When `context.v2.rules.enforceBudget` is unset while resolving nax config, then the resolved `enforceBudget` equals false.
When `context.v2.rules.enforceBudget` is true while resolving nax config, then the resolved `enforceBudget` equals true.

routing.reasoning: A contained multi-file behavior and configuration change with a clear established truncation algorithm.

userStories.title: Report static-rules provider budget pressure
acceptanceCriteria: When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads a canonical store exceeding its `budgetTokens` with `enforceBudget` false, then it returns one chunk per canonical rule, including rules beyond the budget.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads a canonical store exceeding its `budgetTokens` with `enforceBudget` false, then `budgetPressure.overageTokens` equals the store total minus `budgetTokens`.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads a canonical store exceeding its `budgetTokens` with `enforceBudget` false, then `budgetPressure.droppedCount` equals 0.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads a canonical store exceeding its `budgetTokens` with `enforceBudget` true, then `budgetPressure.droppedCount` equals the number of rules omitted from its chunks.

When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads a canonical store exceeding its `budgetTokens` with `enforceBudget` true, then `budgetPressure.droppedTokens` equals the token total of rules omitted from its chunks.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads a canonical store exceeding its `budgetTokens` with `enforceBudget` true, then `budgetPressure.droppedIds` contains the canonical rule ID of every omitted rule.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads canonical rules whose total is within `budgetTokens`, then its result omits `budgetPressure`.
When the canonical loader raises `NeutralityLintError` during `StaticRulesProvider.fetch`, then `fetch` throws that error instead of returning an empty chunk list.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads this repository's `.nax/rules/` store under default configuration, then it returns one chunk per rule file in that store.
When `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` reads this repository's `.nax/rules/` store under default configuration, then `budgetPressure.droppedCount` equals 0.
When no canonical rules exist and `allowLegacyClaudeMd` is false, then `StaticRulesProvider.fetch` returns an empty chunk list and does not use legacy rule files.

userStories.title: Persist and aggregate provider budget pressure
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry provider-reported budget pressure through assembled manifests into bounded per-provider story metrics.

**Motivation** — The provider has no channel to report it: `ContextProviderResult` (`types.ts:543-552`) carries only `chunks` and `pullTools`.

**Approach** —
```text
applyCanonicalRulesBudget(rules, cap, {enforce})
  -> {rules, totalTokens, usedTokens, droppedCount, overageTokens}
       |
StaticRulesProvider.fetch()
  -> ContextProviderResult{chunks, budgetPressure?}
       |
orchestrator provider loop (orchestrator.ts:337-356)
  -> manifest.providerResults[i].budgetPressure
       |
collectStoryMetrics() -> deriveContextMetrics() (tracker.ts:58-80)
  -> StoryMetrics.context.providers[providerId].budgetPressure
```

**Scope** — In: add optional full pressure to persisted `ContextManifest.providerResults`; copy the optional provider-returned value during `assemble()`; add a bounded `{ overageTokens, droppedCount, droppedTokens }` metric and aggregate each field across persisted stage manifests. Out: provider generation/config wiring and the `ContextProviderResult` contract (US-003); type extraction (US-001); ids in story metrics; Changes to the effectiveness classifier, `pollutionRatio`, or the Context Engine v2 write path are deferred. Changes to `packChunks`, `FLOOR_KINDS` membership, floor-overflow semantics, or any per-stage `budgetTokens` value in `stage-config.ts` are deferred. US-004 only: making context-manifest writes atomic against concurrent readers is deferred; this feature adds a field to an existing manifest write and does not change its concurrency behaviour.

**Interface** — `ContextProviderResult.budgetPressure?: ProviderBudgetPressure` (provided by US-003) and `ContextManifest.providerResults[].budgetPressure?: ProviderBudgetPressure` carry the full shape. `ContextProviderMetrics.budgetPressure?` carries only `{ overageTokens, droppedCount, droppedTokens }` — ids stay in the manifest because aggregating them across stages grows unbounded.

`overageTokens` is a deliberately reused name for a distinct measurement. `context.floorOverage.overageTokens` remains per-stage floor-kind overflow beyond `effectiveBudget`; `context.providers[id].budgetPressure.overageTokens` is provider-produced content beyond its own internal budget before packing. A provider can report one while the other is zero, and vice versa. Legacy manifests without `budgetPressure` are treated as no pressure and contribute zero rather than being inferred.

**Failure handling** — A provider result with no `budgetPressure` produces a manifest entry with the field absent; the metrics aggregate omits pressure if none of that provider's stored entries reported it.

**Manifest write path** — `assemble()` does not persist the manifest; it returns it on `ContextBundle.manifest`. The disk write happens in its callers (`src/pipeline/stages/context.ts:203`, `src/context/engine/stage-assembler.ts:229`) via `writeContextManifest`. Assert against the returned bundle's `manifest.providerResults`, not against a file on disk.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a registered context provider whose `fetch` returns `budgetPressure`, when `assemble()` runs, then the returned bundle's `manifest.providerResults` entry for that provider has `budgetPressure` equal to the provider-returned value.

Given a registered context provider whose `fetch` returns no `budgetPressure`, when `assemble()` runs, then the returned bundle's `manifest.providerResults` entry for that provider omits `budgetPressure`.

When `collectStoryMetrics` reads stored stage manifests for a provider with `budgetPressure`, then `context.providers[providerId].budgetPressure.overageTokens` equals the sum of that provider's stored `overageTokens`.

When `collectStoryMetrics` reads stored stage manifests for a provider with `budgetPressure`, then `context.providers[providerId].budgetPressure.droppedCount` equals the sum of that provider's stored `droppedCount`.

When `collectStoryMetrics` reads stored stage manifests for a provider with `budgetPressure`, then `context.providers[providerId].budgetPressure.droppedTokens` equals the sum of that provider's stored `droppedTokens`.
When `collectStoryMetrics` reads stored manifests whose entries for a provider carry no `budgetPressure`, then `context.providers[providerId]` omits `budgetPressure`.
When `collectStoryMetrics` reads legacy stored manifests with no `budgetPressure`, then it contributes zero provider budget pressure rather than inferring one.
When `collectStoryMetrics` reads stored manifest pressure entries containing `droppedIds`, then `context.providers[providerId].budgetPressure` has no `droppedIds` property.

routing.reasoning: This extends the existing provider-results mapping and manifest aggregation loop across five familiar files, with additive optional fields and existing manifest-store test seams.

analysis:
The affected code is an existing Context Engine v2 flow, not a greenfield build. `applyCanonicalRulesBudget` in src/context/rules/canonical-loader.ts:375-402 currently accepts two parameters, drops the contiguous tail whenever accumulated tokens exceed the cap, and returns rules/totalTokens/usedTokens/droppedCount. It has two callers, including `StaticRulesProvider.fetch`. StaticRulesProvider loads, package-filters, overlays, priority-sorts, touched-file-filters, then budgets canonical rules before turning them into static floor chunks (src/context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts:183-294); its options currently expose only legacy fallback and budgetTokens (src/context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts:55-66). The default orchestrator resolves rules config and constructs that provider at src/context/engine/orchestrator-factory.ts:40-44, so enforceBudget must be resolved there and passed explicitly.

Configuration is schema-first: ContextV2RulesConfigSchema defines allowLegacyClaudeMd and budgetTokens and has an object default at src/config/schemas-context.ts:54-68; the root DEFAULT_CONFIG literal independently supplies the same nested object at src/config/schemas.ts:321. Runtime consumers receive ContextV2RulesConfig from src/config/runtime-types-context.ts:48-56. Both default literals must include enforceBudget because Zod object defaults are not re-parsed.

Manifest types and provider contracts are centralized in src/context/engine/types.ts. ContextManifest.providerResults is an optional persisted array at src/context/engine/types.ts:225-267, while ContextProviderResult contains chunks and optional pullTools at src/context/engine/types.ts:543-552. The manifest block begins at src/context/engine/types.ts:123 and the file is near the 600-line source limit, so US-001 must relocate the designated chunk/manifest declarations to manifest-types.ts and re-export them before US-004 adds new documented fields. Consumers include manifest-store (writeContextManifest at src/context/engine/manifest-store.ts:64-74), orchestrator, and tests importing ContextManifest from types.ts; preserving the barrel re-export avoids import-site migration and preserves the persisted JSON schema.

The orchestrator concurrently fetches providers then maps provider status into providerResults (src/context/engine/orchestrator.ts:320-370). It must copy an optional budgetPressure without inventing it for providers that do not report one. Metrics flow is persisted-manifest based: collectStoryMetrics calls module-private deriveContextMetrics when projectDir and feature are available (src/metrics/tracker.ts:138-222); deriveContextMetrics loops every manifest provider result and sums standard provider values (src/metrics/tracker.ts:45-80). ContextProviderMetrics currently carries aggregate production/status/cost fields at src/metrics/types.ts:72-89. Add a bounded aggregate budgetPressure there and sum it only when present; legacy manifests must contribute zero and must not get inferred pressure. The existing computeFloorOverage precedent in src/metrics/tracker.ts:121-136 shows the correct compatibility rule: missing historical fields contribute zero rather than a fabricated fallback. Provider pressure is deliberately distinct from floor overage: provider pressure measures produced content above a provider threshold before packing, whereas floor overage measures floor chunks packed beyond effective stage budget.

Existing test anchors are test/unit/context/rules/canonical-loader.test.ts (canonical budget and loader behaviors), test/unit/context/engine/providers/static-rules.test.ts (provider fixtures and injectable canonical-loader dependency), test/unit/context/engine/manifest-store.test.ts (manifest persistence), test/unit/context/engine/orchestrator.test.ts (assemble/provider integration), test/unit/context/engine/orchestrator-factory.test.ts (config wiring), and test/unit/metrics/tracker-context-metrics.test.ts (multi-stage manifest aggregation using manifest-store dependency injection). Risks are behaviorally intentional default expansion of rules, inadvertent loss of fail-closed NeutralityLintError propagation, omission of either config default literal, conflating two unrelated overage metrics, and breaking old manifest parsing/import compatibility during the type move. Migration is additive and wire-compatible: absent optional budgetPressure represents no recorded pressure; no stored manifest rewrite is required. The dependency order is essential: first make type-file headroom (US-001), independently introduce soft budget/config semantics (US-002), then emit provider pressure (US-003), and finally persist and aggregate it (US-004).
outOfScope: Two-tier rule delivery — an always-on tier carrying every rule's prohibitions plus full text fetched on demand via a `query_rules` pull tool — is deferred to a later arc; it requires authored per-rule summaries and should be designed against measurements this feature produces.

Adding `appliesTo:` scoping to the six currently-unscoped rule files (`config-patterns.md`, `error-handling.md`, `forbidden-patterns.md`, `monorepo-awareness.md`, `project-conventions.md`, `testing-commands.md`) is deferred.

Fixing `ruleMatchesTouchedFiles` returning true when `touchedFiles` is empty (`static-rules.ts:141`), which makes `appliesTo:` inert for stories declaring no context files, is deferred to the scoping arc.
Changes to the effectiveness classifier, `pollutionRatio`, or the Context Engine v2 write path are deferred.
Changes to `packChunks`, `FLOOR_KINDS` membership, floor-overflow semantics, or any per-stage `budgetTokens` value in `stage-config.ts` are deferred.
Reducing the token size of any rule file's content is deferred.
US-004 only: making context-manifest writes atomic against concurrent readers is deferred; this feature adds a field to an existing manifest write and does not change its concurrency behaviour.
